message.content: The central attack surface here is exact divisibility by 576: if any transform coefficient is off by a sign or the deferred-denominator construction is inconsistent, the floor division silently truncates, producing off-by-one or worse ints even when random probes look close. I'll record the highest-risk testable claims.

message.reasoning_content: The central risk: divisibility by 576 of the transformed result for all int8 inputs. This is a mathematical property — if the Winograd construction is exact, y is always divisible. But hand-adapted transforms may be wrong. The most testable claim: full-range random INT8 inputs produce mismatches vs reference (off-by-one or worse) because y is not divisible by 576. Record 2-3 claims.
